subject: storytime
title: The Ugly Duckling
about: Hans Christian Andersen's 1843 tale of the big gray duckling the others say looks odd, who waits out a cold winter alone and finds in spring that he has grown into a swan. It gives first graders a gentle way to talk about teasing, being different and being kind, and the moment he sees himself in the water is a joy to read aloud. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Ask: what could the other ducks have said to be kind to the gray duckling?

book.author: Hans Christian Andersen (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A duckling who looks odd grows up to be a swan.

passage.text:
A mother duck sat on her eggs.
Crack, crack, crack!
Out came her little ducklings.
They were small and yellow.
But one egg was very big.
It hatched last of all.
Out came a big gray duckling.
He did not look like the others.
His mother loved him just the same.
***
The ducklings went for a swim in the pond.
The big gray duckling swam the best of all.
But the other ducks said he looked odd.
That made him sad.
"Nobody wants to play with me," he said.
So he swam far away to find a new home.
***
Soon the leaves fell from the trees.
Then cold winter came.
Snow fell all around.
The duckling found a snug spot in the tall grass.
He waited for spring.
He dreamed of the warm sun.
***
At last, spring came.
The sun was warm again.
He saw three white swans on a big lake.
"They are so beautiful," he said.
He swam over to them.
Then he looked down into the water.
He saw a big white swan!
It was him!
He was a swan, too!
***
"Come and swim with us!" said the swans.
They swam all around him.
The young swan was so happy.
He had new friends at last.
Be kind, because everyone grows in their own way.

cards.note: She sat on them until they hatched, one by one, and the big egg hatched last.

cards.q: Where did the ducklings go for a swim?
cards.note: The gray duckling swam the best of all, even though the others said he looked odd.

cards.q: What came out of the very big egg?
cards.note: The other ducklings were small and yellow; this one was big and gray.

cards.q: What did the duckling see when he looked in the water?
cards.note: It was his own reflection: he had grown into a swan.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Crack, crack, crack: the story starts with the eggs hatching.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The swans asked him to swim with them, and he had new friends at last.

cards.q: How did the duckling feel when the ducks said he looked odd?
cards.note: The story says it plainly; ask what he could do for someone who felt that way.
Be kind, because everyone grows in their own way; the last line says it.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'hatched' mean?
cards.note: Baby birds hatch by cracking the shell open from the inside.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
